chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of Ali ibn Ma'bad, on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abil Hassan Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) that he (peace be upon him) heard his father (peace be upon him) say that he (peace be upon him) said:
God chose Abraham as His friend because he never turned down anyone and never asked anyone but God, the Exalted and Mighty.

key_terms.خَلِيلاً: Intimate friend or close companion of God

ai.seo_question: Why was Prophet Abraham chosen as God's intimate friend (Khalil)?
ai.summary: Imam Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates that Allah’s designation of Ibrahim as His *Khalil* (intimate friend) stems from his absolute monotheistic self-sufficiency, specifically his habit of never rejecting any supplicant and directing all requests solely to Allah. This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, highlights the spiritual ideal of *Tawakkul* (reliance) and *Istighna* (independence from creation), distinguishing the Prophet’s unique status by his consistent engagement with others while remaining spiritually anchored in the Divine. It serves as a practical model for believers to emulate in their own interactions, balancing social generosity with exclusive devotion to God.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 32-4 Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja’far al-Hamadani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali ibn Ma’bad, on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abil Hassan Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) that he (a.s.) heard his father (a.s.) say, “

The Honorable the Exalted God chose Abraham (a.s.) as His friend since he never turned down any needy person without fulfilling his need, and never asked anyone but God for the fulfillment of his own needs.”
